Hello!
We are a team of student researchers at Columbia (like @Anthony Chang who just posted a similar message) working with Professor Henry Yuen, and we wanted to share results in Spectral Graph Theory. We’ve formalized some basic definitions and properties of spectral graph theory for general graphs (some results exist in mathlib but only for SimpleGraph) including results on cheeger inequalities and isoperimetric problems. We also have plans to expand to include results such as the Expander mixing lemma among others. You can take a look at our repository https://github.com/celioboulay/expander-graphs
We’d like to be able to contribute these to CSLib if this is relevant.

Weighted graphs sounds like a nice thing to have in general. Mathlib might like it as a PR. Of course, a bit of work is needed to refine the proofs. Further, positivity of edge weights is probably best factored out as a def. In Chapter1.lean I see that you are assuming the vertex and edge sets are Set.univ. I don’t see why you need that assumption. Further there seem to be unfilled sorries.
#new members > Graph spectral theory in Mathlib — what's the state of play?

thank you for the replies :)
I have written a small draft github:WeightedGraph.lean of defs I believe would be good for WeightedGraphs
do you think this (maybe with more results) is more likely to be a more relevant addition to Mathlib? (also maybe I need to switch to another subject since here is CSlib)

also, I had a question regarding hypothesis usage
for example I have [Fintype α] which is required in some definitions, so I declared
variable [Fintype α]
but then I have to omit [Fintype α] in all the statements not using it, or the compiler is not happy, and I think it is not very clean
I was wondering what the best practice is in such cases. should I add [Fintype α] only in the statements where I need it (there are many) instead of using a variable? or rely on many different sections based on which hypothesis I need
I think you should use [Fintype α] only when it is actually needed. There is no point in making a definition or theorem less general for no good reason.

Celio Boulay said:

do you think this (maybe with more results) is more likely to be a more relevant addition to Mathlib?

This is G.EdgeLabeling ℝ≥0. What makes your definition useful? What have you proven using it? Can you avoid specializing to the reals?
